PeacockDB join optimizer: cost as planned and optimized

tpch: 43 queries, 215 (query, mode) runs — optimized cheaper at 80, dearer at 0, the same at 135; 0 skipped, 0 failed. tpcds: 99 queries, 405 (query, mode) runs — optimized cheaper at 386, dearer at 5, the same at 14; 90 skipped, 0 failed.

Costs of two prototype runs, in pandas' bytes. Each cost is the engine's own function — testdata/cost_model.conf, the one its .cost.txt goldens are made by: Σ multiplier × output bytes per node category — applied to a run of the Python prototype over the sf1 tables. The prototype's rows are the engine's, but its bytes are pandas', not the device's, so these costs compare with each other and with nothing else. non-optimized is the plan as the engine planned it; optimized is all the work the optimizer's pipeline did: the optimized plan's run, each dynamic filter's probe plan and each run a replan stopped. A build such a run made is read back through a memory source, which costs nothing: the build was paid for once, where it was made. ratio = optimized / non-optimized: green below 1, red above.

Engine .cost.txt is the engine's own CPU run's figure (<mode>-mini.cost.txt, Arrow bytes) at the mode named. DuckDB is the duckdb_cost= of <q>.duckdb_cost.txt, bytes materialized at pipeline breakers; the named tpch queries have none. Final ratio (projected) = min over modes of the engine's figure × that mode's ratio / DuckDB's: the engine's bytes as the optimizer is projected to change them, not a measured engine cost — directional only, as on the published report. The row is green at or below 1.4, red above. Rules fired: each rule with the modes where it changed the plan out of the modes run — dynamic filters that narrowed a scan, DPhyp trees cheaper than the plan's order, flips, replans; hover for every count per mode, calls and probes included.
